title: A dense nodal array and machine learning reveal a blind fault zone beneath the San Fernando Valley
summary: A machine-learning workflow analyzed one month of recordings from a 140-station nodal array and located 62 earthquakes, including 36 not in the regional catalog. Their distribution exposes a previously unidentified 5.3 × 4 km blind fault zone about 5 km beneath the southern San Fernando Valley; the small-event cluster is rare in the regional catalog despite a 2014 Mb 4.4 earthquake in the zone.
ai_technology: Previously developed machine-learning seismic phase picker, fine-tuned on similar waveforms, with two-step event association
organization: University of Texas at Austin; University of Houston

evidence.tested: A machine-learning workflow analyzed one month of recordings from a 140-station nodal array and located 62 earthquakes, including 36 not in the regional catalog.
evidence.unknown: This is a one-month temporary-array study reported as an arXiv preprint. The fault-zone dimensions and location are inferred from a small cluster of newly detected microearthquakes, not from direct imaging or a long-term catalog; it informs hazard mapping but does not predict future earthquakes.
evidence.ai_role: The model detected weak earthquake signals and picked seismic phases in high-noise recordings, enabling the expanded local event catalog from which the blind fault-zone cluster was interpreted.
